Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City www.dilq.qov.ph OPINION NO. 90 JUL TERESO O. PANGA Director General Philippine Economic Zone Authority 10th Floor, DoubleDragon Center West Building DD Meridian Park, Macapagal Avenue, Pasay City Dear Director General Panga: This has reference to the request for legal opinion regarding PEZA-registered business enterprises (PEZA RBEs) with their host local govemment units pertaining to whether they are required to secure a Mayor's/business permit and other related permits including the payment of pertinent local business taxes, fees and charges to the LGUs. The Bureau of Local Govemment Finance's (BLGF) in their Memorandum Circular (MC) 001.20201 on the Updated Reminders in the Assessment of Local Business Tax (LBT), Registration, Renewal of Business Permits and Licenses, and the Imposition of Local Taxes, Fees and Charges, provides for the exemption from local taxes of PEZA- Registered Enterprises. Sec. 4 of the aforementioned MC provides the following: 4. PEZA-Registered Enterprises i. A PEZA-registered enterprise, which is granted an incentive under the Income Tax Holiday (ITH), is not exempt from payment of real property tax (RPT) on land and/or buildings. However, an eligible enterprise is entitled to the three-year exemption from payment of the RPT on machinery and equipment for every machinery and equipment it acquires for its operation, at any point of its operation, and not only on those acquired during the start of its operation. ii. If a PEZA-registered enterprise is granted an incentive under the Gross Income Tax (GIT) regime, no taxes, local and national, except for RPT on land owned by developers, shall be imposed on business establishments operating within the ECOZONE. In lieu thereof, five percent (5%) of the gross income eamed shall be paid and remitted as follows: a. Three percent (3%) to the National Govemment; and b. Two percent (2%) which shall be directly remitted by the business establishments to the treasurer's office of the municipality or city where the enterprise is located. I January 2, 2020 "Matino, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

Under Sec. 6.2 of JMC No. 01 Series of 2021, PEZA RBEs do not fall under those exempted from securing business permits, to wit: 6.2 Exemption from securing business permits. Business permits shall not be required from: 6.2. I professionals who, in the practice of their profession, have paid professional taxes in the provinces, city or the Ione municipality within the Metropolitan Manila Area where he/she practices her profession. However, as stipulated under the provisions of DOF- LFC No. 001-2019 dated 12 June 2021 , the professional who maintains an office or clinic for his/her practice shall be issued a business permit at no cost; 6.2.2. individuals or those registered in the Securities and Exchange Commission ("SEC") as One Person Corporation ("OPC") who provides personal services that does not fall under the exercise of a profession; provided further, that the individual does not occupy a permanent work or retail space, whether inside the residence or in any commercial space; 6.2.3 service contractors providing temporary or outsourced services outside the LGU where it is registered its principal office or branch; and 6.2.4 BMBEs pursuant to RA 9178 and RA 10644. For purposes of discussion, it bears to emphasize that business/mayor's permits are different from local taxes. A business permit is used for the purpose of regulating any business or undertaking within the jurisdiction of the LGU, which is essentially an exercise of police power of the State within the contemplation of the general welfare clause of the Local Govemment Code2. While the latter is the one imposed by local government units. Considering the highly technical nature of your inquiry, we deem it apt to endorse the matter to the Department of Finance-Bureau of Local Govemment Finance (BLGF) as it is the authority specifically mandated to supervise the revenue operations of all local government units as provided in Section 2, Chapter l, Title II of Executive Order No. 292 series of 1987. Finally, this opinion of this Department is based solely on the facts and representations narrated from the letter and our appreciation of the same. Further, this opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities and the courts. We hope to have assisted you on this matter. Respectfully yours, BY HO TY OF THE SECRETARY: ATTY. J OUSEL VIC .
